findings.title: Underwater withdraw buffer is FCFS at par, socializing strategy loss onto slow stakers
findings.triageReason: Intended design (confirmed by protocol owner). The underwater buffer pays daily-volume withdrawals at par during transient, mean-reverting underwater dips to avoid sparking panic and to avoid forcing users to realise losses by redeeming shares at the bottom; bank-run / mass-exit is handled separately by migrateOut with pro-rata distribution. The report itself concedes there is no incremental victim (the slow staker is baseline-unchanged vs a no-buffer world). The buffer-at-par path implements the documented invariant 'a non-migrating user cannot be forced to realise a loss', and both of the finding's recommended fixes (block the buffer branch / pro-rata haircut) would defeat that design goal. Reclassified from Medium to intended-design via /review-finding.
